## 2. Project scope

**Data source.** A Google Form ("University Student Performance Analysis Form") circulated to
students at BUET, BRAC and CUET. 230 responses, 22 columns, mostly 5-point Likert items plus a
banded self-reported GPA. Question text is bilingual (English + Bangla).

**Two deliverable pipelines:**

| # | Pipeline | Question it answers | Framing |
|---|----------|--------------------|---------|
| A | **Feature influence** | Which factors actually move academic performance? | Ranking / inference |
| B | **CGPA prediction** | Given a student's answers, predict their CGPA band | Supervised classification |

**Two experiments** (following the WEKA tutorial in `docs/`):

- **Primary** — all features *including* the student's previous CGPA band.
- **Behaviour-focused** — the same features *minus* previous CGPA.

They stay separate and are never merged into one ranking. Previous CGPA dominates any model it
sits in, so the behaviour-only run is what actually answers Pipeline A.

**Target variable.** `current_cgpa_band`, 4 ordered classes:

| Code | Range | n |
|------|-------|---|
| `C0_below_3_20` | below 3.20 | 60 |
| `C1_3_20_to_3_49` | 3.20 – 3.49 | 52 |
| `C2_3_50_to_3_74` | 3.50 – 3.74 | 63 |
| `C3_3_75_plus` | 3.75 and above | 55 |

The form collected GPA as **bands, not numbers** (`Below`, `3.0+`, `3.2+`, `3.5+`, `3.75+`,
`3.9+`). So this is an **ordinal classification** problem, not regression. Any "predict the CGPA
number" output is a band midpoint and must be reported as such.

**Tooling.** Cleaning, EDA and model selection in Python (this repo). The final model comparison
is demonstrated in **WEKA**, because that is what the course requires.

## 4. Known data problem — the existing `cleaned-dataset/` files

`student_performance_primary_clean.csv` and `student_performance_behavior_clean.csv` were
produced by a teammate using ChatGPT. **They are not derived from our raw responses.** Verified:

| Check | Our raw form | Those files |
|-------|--------------|-------------|
| Row count | 230 | 878 |
| Departments | CSE, EEE, ECE, ME, CE, BME, ChE, Arch, URP, MME, NCE, IPE, PMRE, MIE, NAME, WRE | includes **TE, LE, BECM, ESE, IEM, MSE** — none of which appear in a single response |
| Satisfaction column | "satisfied with getting admitted into your university" | named **`kuet_satisfaction`** — no KUET student is in our data |
| Semester values | 1–12 | S1–S7 only |
| Row alignment | — | GPA bands do not match the raw data row-for-row |

The department list and the `kuet_` prefix are KUET's, so this is a different (likely synthetic)
dataset. **It must not be used for any result we report.** The *schema* it uses is good and we
kept it — the C0–C3 band scheme, the primary/behaviour split, the snake_case naming — but the
rows are rebuilt from `raw-data/` by our notebook.

`docs/WEKA_Next_Steps_Tutorial.pdf` inherits the same problem: it says "check that WEKA shows 878
instances". For us that number is **230**. Its methodology (ZeroR/OneR baselines, 10-fold CV,
macro-F1, kappa, confusion matrix, gap analysis) is sound and we follow it.

## 5. Preprocessing decisions (each needs a *why* for the viva)

| Decision | Why |
|----------|-----|
| Merge department column with the "if not listed" write-in column | They are complementary, not duplicated (174 + 56 = 230). Dropping either loses a quarter of the column. |
| Canonicalise `BUET/Buet`, `BRAC/Brac/BRAc/BRAC University/BRAC UNI` | Free-text casing variants — 9 raw strings collapse to 3 real universities. |
| Canonicalise department abbreviations (`ChE`→Chemical, `NAME`→Naval Arch. & Marine, …) | The same department written two ways splits its signal across two categories. |
| Missing "responsibilities hours" (44 rows) → `none`, **not** dropped | The question offers no zero option (`1-5`, `6-10`, `11-15`, `>15`). A blank almost certainly means "I have none". Missingness is spread evenly across universities and GPA bands, so it is not a response-quality artefact. Dropping would throw away 19% of the data. |
| Likert → **ordinal integer codes**, not one-hot | The categories are ordered. One-hot destroys that order and inflates dimensionality on n=230. |
| `semester` treated as **not comparable across universities** | BRAC is on trimesters (all its respondents sit at 10–11), CUET's respondents are all at 7, BUET spreads 1–12. The raw semester number encodes *university*, not progress. We derive a normalised progress feature instead. |
| 6 GPA bands collapsed to 4 classes | Matches the C0–C3 scheme and balances the classes (60/52/63/55). Six classes on n=230 leaves ~26 per class. |
| Repeated stratified 10-fold CV, never a single holdout | n=230. One 20% test split is 46 rows — far too noisy to rank models. |

## 7. Conventions for AI agents working in this repo

**Reading PDFs — convert to Markdown first.** Do not read a PDF page-by-page as images; it burns
tokens. Use markitdown (installed in the venv):

```powershell
.\venv\Scripts\python.exe -m markitdown docs\SomeFile.pdf > docs\SomeFile.md
```

Then read the `.md`. Keep the `.md` beside the PDF so the conversion happens only once. If a
`markitdown` **skill** is installed later, prefer the skill; the CLI above is the fallback and is
what currently works in this project.

**Generating slides.** Use the **`frontend-slides`** skill (installed from the
`zarazhangrui/frontend-slides` marketplace). It produces single-file HTML decks on a fixed
1920×1080 stage — not `.pptx`. Three decks already exist in `presentation/`; see §9.

Slides are **generated from data, never hand-written.** All copy and numbers live in
`presentation/build/pres_content.py`, which is transcribed from `docs/results_summary.json`,
`docs/model_results_*.csv` and the notebook. If the notebook is re-run and a number changes,
update `pres_content.py` and rebuild — never edit a generated `.html` by hand.

**Explaining anything to the team.** Use the **`noob-explain`** skill for reports, docs and
walkthrough guides. Everything in `docs/` that a teammate reads should be diagram-first and in
plain English — black box first, then modules. Teammates are being viva'd on this; a doc they
cannot explain out loud is a failed doc.

**Non-negotiables.**
- `raw-data/` is read-only. Every cleaning step lives in the notebook, never in a manual CSV edit.
- No result gets reported that a teammate cannot explain the *why* of.
- Report weak or negative findings honestly. A behaviour-only model that barely beats ZeroR is a
  real finding about self-reported survey data, not a failure to be hidden.
- No causal claims. This is cross-sectional self-reported data — "associated with", never "causes".

## 8. Presentation decks

Three complete decks of the same 13 slides, in three visual styles, for the team to pick from.
Open any of them in a browser — no build step, no internet needed for anything but webfonts.

| File | Style |
|------|-------|
| `presentation/deck-signal.html` | Navy + cream + antique gold, editorial serif |
| `presentation/deck-cobalt.html` | Cream graph-paper, electric cobalt, Newsreader serif |
| `presentation/deck-swiss.html` | White / black / red, Archivo Black, visible grid |

**Controls.** Arrow keys, Space, PageUp/Down, Home/End; mouse wheel; swipe on touch. `E` toggles
inline editing — click any text, edit it, `Ctrl+S` saves to that browser's localStorage. Each
deck deep-links by slide (`#slide-7`).

**Rebuilding.**

```powershell
cd presentation\build
..\..\venv\Scripts\python.exe build.py all     # regenerate all three
..\..\venv\Scripts\python.exe verify.py all    # check every slide fits the 1920x1080 stage
```

`verify.py` renders all 39 slides in headless Chromium and fails on content overflow, escaping
elements, overlapping panels, text under 14px, decorations covering text, and a stage that stops
being 16:9 on a phone. Run it after any content or theme change.

Source layout: `pres_content.py` (all copy and numbers), `slides_html.py` (shared semantic
markup), `theme_*.py` (one stylesheet per style), `deck_shell.py` (fixed-stage CSS + controller),
`build.py`, `verify.py`. Screenshots land in `build/shots/<deck>/`.

> The work-distribution table on slide 13 is a **placeholder** — confirm who did what and edit it
> (press `E` in the deck, or change `pres_content.py` and rebuild).
